title: The Great Schism
objective: After this level you can explain why the Church split into East and West in 1054.
summary: In 1054 a papal legate and the patriarch of Constantinople excommunicated each other, the traditional date of the East-West split, after centuries of drifting apart.

cards.headline: In 1054 a cardinal walked into Hagia Sophia and excommunicated a patriarch.
cards.body: It was July 16, and the pope who had sent him was already dead. Did one day in July really split Christianity in two?

cards.headline: Excommunication, returned
cards.body: Remember Justinian’s great church from Level 5? That’s where it happened. The papal legate Cardinal Humbert excommunicated Patriarch Michael Cerularius and his clergy. Cerularius called a synod and excommunicated the pope’s envoys right back. These mutual excommunications became a watershed in church history, the traditional date for the split between the Latin West and the Orthodox East. A slammed door, heard for centuries.

cards.headline: Drifting apart
cards.body: But the two churches had been drifting apart since the 5th century. The East never accepted Rome’s growing claim to lead the whole Church. Rome had added “and the Son” to the Creed without consulting the East. Easterners also resented Roman rules on celibate clergy and unleavened bread at the Eucharist. And Level 4’s eastern empire had swapped Latin for Greek in government. 1054 was less an explosion than the end of a long, slow drift.

mascot.line: People picture 1054 as a sudden split. Think centuries of drift, then a slammed door.

cards.headline: Undoing 1054
cards.body: The excommunications themselves stood until 1965, when Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I held simultaneous ceremonies revoking them. That’s 911 years to take back one July’s work.

cards.headline: The Great Schism: understood
learned: In 1054 legate and patriarch excommunicated each other
The churches had drifted apart since the 5th century

questions.prompt: Put these steps in the story of 1054 in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Cardinal Humbert excommunicated Patriarch Michael Cerularius. Cerularius called a synod and excommunicated the pope’s envoys right back. In 1965 simultaneous ceremonies revoked the excommunications.

questions.prompt: Why do historians see the split between East and West as gradual rather than sudden?

options.label: Nobody in Constantinople heard about 1054
options.rationale: It happened in Hagia Sophia itself.

options.label: The churches had been drifting apart since the 5th century
The split only began in 1965
options.rationale: That was when the excommunications were lifted.

questions.explanation: Relations had been a growing estrangement from the 5th to the 11th century, over authority, the Creed and customs.

questions.prompt: The 1054 excommunication was delivered in Hagia Sophia, a church built by _____.

options.label: Theodoric
options.rationale: He was a Gothic king in Italy.

options.label: Clovis
options.rationale: He was king of the Franks.

questions.explanation: Justinian had Hagia Sophia built after the Nika riots; it was completed in 537.
